_comment: Bible designer, axis 4 of 5 (story/designer/INTERVIEW.md): what changes from chapter to chapter. Changing numbers are logged as Stat Changes rows (an event per change), never overwritten in a cell: 'Chapter 23: Kira gains 500 XP' beats editing a number. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY.
goal: Know which values change over chapters, which of them are numbers, which way they may move, their floors and ceilings, and what the page prints.

questions.ask: As the chapters go by, what changes — numbers, possessions, who someone answers to, what they know?
questions.why: Each answer is a column that changes over chapters, so 'as of chapter 12' has an answer.
questions.listenFor: levels, stats, money, strength, who holds an item, loyalties

questions.ask: Which of those are numbers? For each: can it ever go down? Is there a floor or a ceiling?
questions.why: A number that never goes down gets a direction the checker enforces; a floor or ceiling becomes min and max.
questions.listenFor: 'it never drops', 'it can go negative', 'it caps at 10'

questions.ask: Does the page ever show these numbers — a status screen, a ledger, a report, a muster roll?
questions.why: Each number the page prints becomes a printed row, checked against the running total, so a status box that disagrees with the story is caught.
questions.listenFor: status boxes, character sheets, official counts quoted in the text

questions.ask: Are some changes temporary or conditional — while something is worn, until a certain chapter, only at night?
questions.why: A change that only holds sometimes is the most common source of a number drifting; it is logged with its condition, never folded in silently.
Starting values are chapter-0 set rows; every later change is counted from them.
questions.listenFor: numbers for the main people at the start of the book; in nonfiction, the source that gives them

doneWhen: Every changing number is named, has its direction, floor and ceiling if any, and a starting value (or is marked to look up).
